nodes.notes: Starts the workflow on a timer — every 2 h. No input data; downstream nodes fetch what they need.

On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run. Credential: API key / bearer for the target API. Whatever the target API issues — usually a bearer token or API key.

nodes.name: Normalize Records
nodes.notes: Custom JavaScript: Normalize incoming record records to a stable schema Watch out: Must return an array of items shaped like [{ json: {...} }].

nodes.name: Fingerprint for Idempotency
nodes.notes: Custom JavaScript: Build a stable idempotency key per record (djb2 hash, no deps) Watch out: Must return an array of items shaped like [{ json: {...} }].

nodes.name: Drop Already-Processed Items
nodes.notes: Cross-execution dedupe: remembers keys it has processed before and drops repeats — the idempotency guard. Watch out: Cross-execution memory persists. After changing the key field, clear stored keys or old keys keep matching.

nodes.name: Upsert into HubSpot
nodes.notes: Creates or updates a HubSpot contact by email — HubSpot is the CRM system of record for this pipeline. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run. Credential: HubSpot private-app token. HubSpot → Settings → Integrations → Private Apps → create app → copy the token.

nodes.name: Advance Watermark
nodes.notes: Custom JavaScript: Advance the incremental watermark to the newest record seen Watch out: Must return an array of items shaped like [{ json: {...} }].

nodes.name: Persist Watermark (Google Sheets)
nodes.notes: Upserts a row into 'Record Tracker', matched on recordId — re-running with the same key updates the row instead of duplicating it. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run. Credential: Google OAuth2 / service account. Google Cloud Console → enable Sheets API → OAuth2 client, or a Service Account.

nodes.name: Row Counts Match?
nodes.notes: Two-way gate on ={{ $json.processed >= 0 }}. TRUE continues the happy path, FALSE takes the alternate branch. Watch out: The false branch carries the non-matching items — wire it deliberately rather than leaving it dangling.

parameters.text: =⚠️ ETL drift detected: {{ $json.processed }} rows vs expected

nodes.name: Raise Drift Alarm
nodes.notes: Sends a Telegram message to the configured chat — the same bot can also receive replies, so this doubles as a two-way ops channel. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run. Credential: Telegram bot token. Message @BotFather on Telegram → /newbot → copy the token.

nodes.name: Stamp Completion Time
nodes.notes: Stamps completedAt with the current time for auditing.

nodes.name: Persist Run Metadata
nodes.notes: Saves key fields onto the execution record — searchable later in n8n's execution list.

nodes.name: Load Previous Snapshot 2
nodes.notes: Searches Airtable's 'Records' table by formula (={LastModified} > DATEADD(NOW(), -1, 'days')) for records the pipeline hasn't handled yet. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. nodes.name: Compute Drift vs Snapshot
nodes.notes: Custom JavaScript: Compare current metrics with the previous snapshot Watch out: Must return an array of items shaped like [{ json: {...} }].

# Sync contacts across systems: Telegram

**Pattern:** Two-System Sync · **Level:** Advanced · **Trigger:** Scheduled

## Overview

Runs on a schedule, and covers two-way-sync work end to end across Telegram, Google Sheets, HubSpot and Airtable.

It moves through 20 working steps plus a 3-node error rail, in this order:

1. Hourly Schedule
2. Load Previous Snapshot
3. Fetch Changes Since Watermark
4. Normalize Records
5. Fingerprint for Idempotency
6. Drop Already-Processed Items
7. Upsert into HubSpot
8. Advance Watermark
9. Persist Watermark (Google Sheets)
10. Row Counts Match?
11. Raise Drift Alarm
12. Stamp Completion Time
13. Persist Run Metadata
14. Load Previous Snapshot 2
15. Compute Drift vs Snapshot
16. Enrich with Reference Data
17. Fold In Enrichment Fields
18. Summarize Run Stats
19. Append Audit Row (HubSpot)
20. Send Summary to Telegram

Anything that throws leaves the happy path at that node and goes down the red rail — Capture Failure Context → Escalate Failure to Telegram → Park in Dead-Letter Queue — so a failure is reported rather than silently lost.

## Why it exists

Doing two-way-sync work by hand is slow and easy to get wrong, and it stops entirely when the person who does it is away. This makes the process repeatable and monitored, with failures surfaced instead of silently lost.

## Main flow

Hourly Schedule → Load Previous Snapshot → Fetch Changes Since Watermark → Normalize Records → Fingerprint for Idempotency → Drop Already-Processed Items → Upsert into HubSpot → Advance Watermark → Persist Watermark (Google Sheets) → Row Counts Match? → Raise Drift Alarm → Stamp Completion Time → Persist Run Metadata → Load Previous Snapshot 2 → Compute Drift vs Snapshot → Enrich with Reference Data → Fold In Enrichment Fields → Summarize Run Stats → Append Audit Row (HubSpot) → Send Summary to Telegram → Capture Failure Context → Escalate Failure to Telegram → Park in Dead-Letter Queue

## Use it for

- Teams keeping Telegram and Google Sheets aligned by hand for two-way sync
- Two-way sync work where "Fetch Changes Since Watermark" is still a manual step before Telegram
- Two-way sync work that only reaches Telegram on a schedule, when someone remembers to start it

## You get

- Keeps Telegram and Google Sheets in step for two-way sync, without anyone re-typing a row
- Safe to re-run: records already in Telegram or Google Sheets are skipped, across all 23 nodes of this two-way-sync build
- A failed Telegram or Google Sheets call is retried rather than dropped, at any of the 23 nodes in this two-way-sync build
- Every two-way-sync run leaves an audit row behind, alongside Telegram
- Fans the same result out to HubSpot in the same run, for two-way sync

## Before first run
Connect credentials: API key / bearer for the target API; Airtable PAT; Google OAuth2 / service account; HubSpot private-app token; Telegram bot token.
Follow the color key: 🟦 entry · 🟪 AI · 🟫 actions · ⬜ utilities · 🟩 outputs · 🟥 error rail.
Each node has its own doc card underneath — read those before editing.

## Try it now
Sample data is pinned on the trigger — hit **Execute Workflow** to watch it flow through every node before connecting any real credentials. Unpin the trigger (right-click → Unpin) when you're ready to go live.

## Design decisions

The pipeline is incremental, not full-refresh: it stores a watermark (the last-seen timestamp) and only asks the source for records newer than that, which is what keeps a scheduled re-run cheap instead of re-pulling the entire dataset every time. The tradeoff is that a failed watermark write must be safe to retry — which is exactly why the destination write is an upsert, not a plain insert.

## Practice exercises

Already production-grade — deepen your understanding:

1. Manually roll the watermark back and re-run — confirm the upsert makes the replay safe (no duplicates).
2. Trigger a reconcile mismatch on purpose and confirm the drift alarm fires.
3. Point the source at a different platform and see how little else in the workflow has to change.

## Credentials setup

Credentials are never included in a template file, so every node below needs its own connection before the first real run. In n8n: open the node, click the Credential dropdown, choose **Create new**.

**Google OAuth2 / service account**
Google Cloud Console → enable Sheets API → OAuth2 client, or a Service Account.
_Gotcha:_ Using a Service Account? Share the spreadsheet with its email address or it 404s.

**API key / bearer for the target API**
Whatever the target API issues — usually a bearer token or API key.
_Gotcha:_ Store it as a credential, never typed into the node's parameters.

**HubSpot private-app token**
HubSpot → Settings → Integrations → Private Apps → create app → copy the token.
_Gotcha:_ Grant the CRM scopes you need; legacy API keys are deprecated and will not work.

**Telegram bot token**
Message @BotFather on Telegram → /newbot → copy the token.
_Gotcha:_ Get your chat ID by messaging the bot then opening api.telegram.org/bot<TOKEN>/getUpdates.

**Airtable PAT**
airtable.com/create/tokens → create a Personal Access Token.
_Gotcha:_ Scope the token to the specific base, and grant `data.records:write`. Field names are case-sensitive.

Set each credential up once and it is reusable across every workflow in your instance.

## Troubleshooting

**Workflow does nothing when the trigger should fire**
Cause: It is still a draft, or the trigger is inactive.
Fix: Publish/activate the workflow. Manual test runs use a different URL than production.

**A node shows a red error triangle on import**
Cause: No credential is attached yet.
Fix: Expected on a fresh import — open the node and attach a credential (see the Credentials setup note).

**HTTP node returns 401 or 403**
Cause: Wrong or unscoped credential, or the API expects a header this request isn't sending.
Fix: Verify the key directly with curl first, then confirm the auth type matches what the API documents.

**HTTP node returns 429**
Cause: Rate limited by the provider.
Fix: Raise the wait between calls or lower the batch size. Retries already back off, but they cannot beat a hard quota.

Still stuck? n8n's **Executions** tab shows the exact node that failed and the data going into it — start there rather than guessing.

## 🛟 Error handling & retries

External calls retry **3× with 2s backoff**. Anything still failing exits through its node's error output into the red error rail → context is captured and the on-call channel is alerted. Failures are also parked in a dead-letter queue for replay. Set an n8n **Error Workflow** in settings as the final safety net.

## 🧹 Data quality

Dedupe/diff steps make re-runs safe: the same input twice will not create duplicate records. If you change the key fields, clear n8n's dedupe memory (node → 'Clear stored keys') before the next run.

## 🛠 Customize me

Quick wins: point the data nodes at your own accounts (see 🔑 lines on each card), adjust the trigger cadence, and tune thresholds/labels to your two-way sync process. Every node card explains its role — safe to extend at any marked branch.

## 🔐 Security

Credentials live in n8n's credential store and are never written into node parameters — that is why this file carries none.

**Least privilege for this build**
- Telegram: the bot token is a bearer credential — rotate it if it ever appears in an execution log.
- Google Sheets: share the single spreadsheet with the service account rather than granting drive-wide access.
- HubSpot: a private-app token carrying only the CRM scopes these nodes use — legacy API keys are deprecated and over-broad.
- Airtable: scope the PAT to this one base and to `data.records:write`; a token scoped to the workspace can rewrite every base.

The HTTP node sends a secret: keep it in a header credential, never in the URL — query strings land in proxy and execution logs.

**Do not log**
Log the identifier and the outcome, not the whole two-way-sync payload. n8n stores execution data verbatim, so anything a node emits is readable by everyone with instance access.
